repo-scanner-bot: automated alert — plaintext SSH deploy key discovered in build artifact for repo redwood/edge-proxy at commit abc123, artifact s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/edge-proxy/2026-06-15/abc123.tar.gz :eyes:
jamie: copying. can someone revoke the deploy key and rotate any hosts that might have been accessed?
maria: tagging infra — do we know which envs used that key? prod/staging/dev?
nick: initial check: key comment shows `deploy@ci-runner`, likely used by ci-runner-05 which has access to staging only. i'm revoking the github deploy key now.
nick: `gh api repos/redwood/edge-proxy/keys -X DELETE -f id=4521` -> 204 No Content via GH app (key id 4521) :white_check_mark:
arjun: good. we should assume any artifact containing a private key is compromised. rotate any service accounts or host keys that used it. i'll run a search across all CI artifacts and build logs for private-key PEM markers.
arjun: running quick grep on artifacts bucket: `gsutil cat gs://redwood-ci-artifacts/** | grep -E "BEGIN (OPENSSH|RSA) PRIVATE KEY" -n || true`
jamie: also check KMS/decryption logs to see if anyone attempted to use the key material elsewhere. if this was uploaded by mistake, we need to know accessors.
maria: who can pull CloudTrail/Audit logs for S3/GCS access during 2026-06-14..15 window? security-oncall?
security-oncall: i'm on it. pulling CloudTrail and GCS audit logs now, will report any GetObject / Download events.
repo-scanner-bot: contextual info — CI job 9876 uploaded artifact at 2026-06-15T03:12:04Z, triggered by pipeline `deploy-staging` on runner ci-runner-05. job logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/9876/logs
nick: taken immediate containment steps: (1) deleted GitHub deploy key (done), (2) removed artifact from public/accessible S3 path and moved to sealed quarantine bucket, (3) disabled ci-runner-05 in fleet.
jamie: add RBAC change: restrict which CI jobs can upload artifacts with wide read ACLs. ticket this: ENGSEC-312.
arjun: results of grep across artifacts: found the PEM marker in 7 artifacts across 3 repos (edge-proxy, infra/ansible, onboarding-scripts). listing attached in secure ticket.
maria: infra note — if hosts used that key for SSH auth, rotate authorized_keys and issue new certs. check our SSH bastion logs for sshd auth using that key fingerprint.
security-oncall: CloudTrail shows two GetObject events from IP 34.82.11.90 during the window. the source ASN is our CI fleet IP range, no external downloads seen so far. continuing timeline analysis.
jamie: plan (short): 1) revoke key + rotate all keys that referenced it (in hosts, deploy agents). 2) rotate any service tokens that the compromised runner could access. 3) full leak-scan across repos and build logs. 4) tighten CI artifact retention + scrub sensitive files before upload. 5) postmortem + communication.
maria: can we add an immediate pre-commit/CI lint that blocks `BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY` from being added to artifacts? this should be a 1-day fix.
nick: quick workaround added to runners — before upload we now run `grep -q -E "BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY" $ARTIFACT || true` and fail uploads; pushing change to runner image.
arjun: will open a follow-up task to integrate our repo-scanner into the CI pipeline so scans run pre-upload rather than async.
security-oncall: evidence collection saved to secure incident folder, created INC-2026-042. will prepare a short blameless write-up for the post-incident review.
jamie: thanks all. assign owners for rotation: nick -> github/app & deploy keys, maria -> host cert rotation, arjun -> artifact scanner integration, security-oncall -> audit log timeline and incident report. please update the ticket with times and commands used.
repo-scanner-bot: closing note — running org-wide leak-scan across all public and private repos now, will post results in ENGSEC-312 when complete. :lock:
